rules.title: No async void
rules.description: Async methods must return Task/ValueTask and end with 'Async'. async void is only allowed for event handlers.

rules.title: No sync-over-async
rules.description: Never block with .Result, .Wait() or .GetAwaiter().GetResult() on a Task; await it instead (deadlocks, thread-pool starvation).

rules.title: Dispose resources
rules.description: IDisposable/IAsyncDisposable instances must be wrapped in using/await using. Do not new up HttpClient per call; use IHttpClientFactory.

rules.title: Do not swallow exceptions
rules.description: No empty catch blocks. Catch the narrowest exception type; if catching Exception, log and rethrow (use 'throw;' not 'throw ex;').

rules.title: Propagate CancellationToken
rules.description: Public async APIs that perform I/O accept a CancellationToken and pass it to every downstream call.

rules.title: Parameterised SQL only
rules.description: Never build SQL by string concatenation or interpolation with external input; use parameters, EF Core LINQ or stored procedures.

rules.title: Validate public inputs
rules.description: Public methods validate reference arguments (ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull) and ranges before use.

rules.title: Structured logging, no secrets
rules.description: Use ILogger message templates (not string interpolation). Never log secrets, tokens, passwords or personal/health data.

rules.title: Dependency injection
rules.description: Use constructor injection. No service locator, no static mutable state, no 'new' of services that have dependencies.

rules.title: Keep methods small
rules.description: Methods over ~50 lines or with deep nesting / high cyclomatic complexity should be split.
